item: Cu-family test sieve No. 60 (250 um scalp)
pack: 1 sieve, 8 in dia x 2 in deep, 304 stainless frame and cloth, ASTM E11 No. 60
qty_basis: 1 per Cu-family stack: today the lab has one stack (Al); a second set is 1 of each piece
notes: Lab spec: DAL's 8 in x 2 in, 304 stainless McMaster stack, No. 60, 100, 140, 230, 325 + pan (instruments_char.py STACK and its DAL PR #175 comment; notes/instruments_char.md; notes/alloy_print.md: McMaster 7969T42, T43, T48 arrived Nov 4). Priority 'soon': waits on Sterling's call on whether to dedicate sieve sets per family now. Bare 304 stainless, so the colour is the 12 mm band on our stainless handling tab (sieve_station.py), not the sieve. Washed in ultrasonic IPA and dried at no more than 60 C (Retsch's limit is 80 C), so the band must take IPA and warm air. McMaster's own page says the series is made in Germany and meets ASTM E11. Gilson alt: all stainless, full height, stacked height 2-1/8 in vs McMaster's 2 in. The tab, stand, tipper and wash fixtures are drawn to the McMaster profile (50.8 mm per sieve), so use Gilson only for hand sieving, or re-check those fixtures first. McMaster's table gives no delivery date. 7969T42's own page said 'Delivers Tuesday'.

item: Cu-family Al-powder funnel (printed PP, white, band with 'Al')
qty_basis: charge.FUNNEL_LABEL has 5 powders. Only Al is in both families: the Al family's base (AlSi10Mg top-up) and about 9-10 wt% of the Cu family's NAB (C95800) and 630 bronze (C63000). Si is Al-family only (Al-10Si, 4047, AlSi10Mg). Ni, Fe and Cu are Cu-family only (Cu-10Ni, NAB, 630). So 1 extra funnel
notes: Our design (charge.py: 36 mm tall, 40 mm mouth, 9/6 mm stem, 28 mm flange, 42 x 6 mm band), printed in-house, so no unit price. No PP filament price was fetched: Polymaker's PolyLite PP page returns 404 and MatterHackers' PP list didn't render. A 3DJake search snippet shows FormFutura white PP 500 g at $32.11 (snippet), about $0.30 a funnel. Caveats: the AlSi10Mg funnel and a pure-Al funnel for bronze are different powders, so 'one funnel per powder' already gives the Cu family its own. Also, notes/lab_r8.md says plastics are the worst for charge build-up with Al powder (NFPA 484, Aluminum Association TR-2), so consider a dissipative print material for both Al funnels. It needs a second fork on charge.funnel_stand.
